q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-01#question: Which peace settlement ended the Thirty Years' War in 1648?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-01#explanatio: The Peace of Westphalia, negotiated in Münster and Osnabrück, ended the war in 1648.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-02#question: Which king made Versailles the seat of his court and was known as the Sun King?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-02#explanatio: Louis XIV moved the court to Versailles in 1682 and, as the Sun King, became the embodiment of absolutism.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-03#question: What did Isaac Newton describe in his Principia of 1687?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-03#choices.3: The laws of motion and gravitation
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-03#explanatio: With his laws of motion and his law of gravitation, Newton explained the movement of bodies on Earth and in space.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-04#question: Which city did Peter the Great found in 1703 as the new capital of Russia?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-04#explanatio: St. Petersburg on the Neva became the capital in 1712 and was regarded as Russia's window on Europe.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-05#question: Which two powers were on the same side in the Seven Years' War (1756 to 1763)?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-05#explanatio: Prussia under Frederick II and Great Britain fought together against Austria, France and Russia.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-06#question: With which motto did Immanuel Kant sum up the program of the Enlightenment?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-06#choices.1: Have the courage to use your own understanding
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-06#explanatio: In 1784 Kant defined enlightenment as the emergence from self-imposed immaturity and chose Sapere aude as its motto.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-07#question: Why was Galileo Galilei condemned by the Inquisition in 1633?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-07#choices.0: Because he had invented the telescope
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-07#choices.1: Because he had translated the Bible into Italian
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-07#choices.2: Because he had defended the heliocentric view of the universe
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-07#explanatio: In his Dialogue of 1632 Galileo had supported the teaching of Copernicus that the Earth moves around the Sun; he was forced to recant.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-08#question: What happened to the English king Charles I in 1649?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-08#choices.1: He was condemned by Parliament and executed
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-08#explanatio: After the civil war a court of Parliament convicted the king of high treason; he was beheaded on January 30, 1649.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-09#question: Which demand is associated with Montesquieu's work The Spirit of the Laws (1748)?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-09#explanatio: Montesquieu called for the legislative, executive and judicial powers to be separated so that they would limit one another.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-10#question: What was the consequence of the Edict of Fontainebleau of 1685?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-10#choices.0: The founding of the Royal Society
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-10#choices.1: The move of the court to Versailles
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-10#choices.2: The beginning of the War of the Spanish Succession
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-10#choices.3: The flight of some 200,000 Huguenots from France
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-10#explanatio: Louis XIV revoked the Edict of Nantes and banned Protestant worship; many Huguenots fled, among other places to Brandenburg.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-11#question: Which country sealed itself off almost completely from the outside world from 1639 onward and allowed only the Dutch to trade on the island of Dejima?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-11#explanatio: The Tokugawa shogunate banned Christianity and restricted foreign trade to Nagasaki; this policy is called sakoku.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-12#question: Which achievement is associated with the physicist Émilie du Châtelet?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-12#choices.0: The discovery of the moons of Jupiter
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-12#choices.1: The French translation and explanation of Newton's Principia
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-12#explanatio: Du Châtelet translated Newton's main work into French and added commentaries; her version is still regarded as authoritative today.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-13#question: Which event triggered the Thirty Years' War in 1618?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-13#explanatio: Protestant Bohemian nobles threw imperial governors out of a window of Prague Castle; the conflict grew into a European war.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-14#question: Which Jesuit criticized the use of torture in witch trials in his 1631 work Cautio Criminalis?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-14#explanatio: Spee showed that torture extracted false confessions; even so, the witch trials only ended in the 18th century.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-15#question: What did Galileo Galilei discover with his telescope in 1610?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-15#explanatio: Galileo published the discovery in 1610 in the Starry Messenger; it supported the Copernican view because clearly not everything revolved around the Earth.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-16#question: Who ruled England as Lord Protector from 1653?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-16#explanatio: Cromwell's New Model Army had defeated the king in the civil war; after Cromwell's death the monarchy returned under Charles II in 1660.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-17#question: Whom did English nobles and politicians invite to England in the Glorious Revolution of 1688?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-17#explanatio: William and his wife Mary became joint rulers, while the Catholic James II fled to France almost without a fight.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-18#question: Which right did the Bill of Rights of 1689 secure for the English Parliament?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-18#choices.0: The right to declare war without the king
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-18#explanatio: It also guaranteed free elections and freedom of speech in Parliament; England thus became a constitutional monarchy.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-19#question: Which rights should a government protect according to John Locke?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-19#explanatio: According to Locke, a government that violates these natural rights may be removed; the idea shaped the American Declaration of Independence.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-20#question: Which thinker concluded from the social contract that a strong, unrestricted ruler was necessary?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-20#explanatio: In Leviathan (1651) Hobbes described the state of nature as a war of all against all; Locke and Rousseau, by contrast, drew liberal conclusions from the idea of a contract.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-21#question: What was the Royal Society's motto 'Nullius in verba' meant to express?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-21#choices.0: Only experiment and observation count as proof
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-21#choices.2: The king stands above all scholars
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-21#choices.3: The Bible is the highest authority
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-21#explanatio: The motto means 'on nobody's word'; the society, founded in 1660, has published the Philosophical Transactions since 1665.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-22#question: Which minister of Louis XIV stands for the economic policy of mercantilism?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-22#explanatio: Colbert promoted manufactories for luxury goods such as tapestries and mirrors, protected domestic production with tariffs and expanded trade and the navy.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-23#question: By what did mercantilism measure the wealth of a state?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-23#choices.2: Its stock of gold and silver
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-23#explanatio: That is why a state was supposed to export more than it imported; colonies served as sources of raw materials and as markets.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-24#question: What was the name of the revolt of the nobility and the Parlement of Paris that Louis XIV experienced as a child?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-24#explanatio: The Fronde (1648–1653) strengthened Louis's resolve to later bind the nobility to the court at Versailles and strip it of political power.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-25#question: How was the power of the absolute king mainly justified?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-25#choices.0: He had been elected by the people
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-25#choices.1: He had been confirmed by parliament
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-25#choices.2: He had been chosen by the nobility
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-25#choices.3: He had been appointed by God
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-25#explanatio: Bishop Bossuet taught that no one could call the king to account; in practice, however, estates and privileges remained in place.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-26#question: Who besieged Vienna for the second time, unsuccessfully, in 1683?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-26#explanatio: After the siege failed, Austria pushed the Ottomans back and rose to become a great power in southeastern Europe.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-27#question: Which Austrian province did Frederick II of Prussia conquer after invading it in 1740?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-27#explanatio: In the War of the Austrian Succession Maria Theresa held on to her other lands but had to leave Silesia to Prussia in the Peace of Aachen in 1748.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-28#question: Which reform did Maria Theresa introduce in her lands in 1774?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-28#explanatio: After the defeat by Prussia Maria Theresa reformed the administration, army and taxes; as a devout Catholic, however, she rejected religious toleration.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-29#question: How did Frederick II of Prussia describe himself?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-29#choices.0: As the first servant of his state
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-29#choices.2: As the father of the revolution
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-29#explanatio: Frederick abolished torture and granted religious toleration but held on to noble privileges and his unrestricted power.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-30#question: Which crop caught on in Prussia in the 18th century despite resistance and reduced famines?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-30#explanatio: The tuber from the Americas yielded a lot of food on a small area; at the same time the agricultural revolution with new crop rotations began in England.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-31#question: Where did the Russian empress Catherine the Great come from?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-31#explanatio: Born Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst, she converted to the Orthodox faith and overthrew her husband Peter III in 1762 with the help of the guards.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-32#question: Who led the great uprising of peasants and Cossacks against Catherine II in 1773?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-32#explanatio: After the Pugachev rebellion Catherine strengthened the rights of the nobility and extended serfdom even further.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-33#question: Which powers divided parts of Poland among themselves for the first time in 1772?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-33#choices.3: Austria, the Ottoman Empire and Russia
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-33#explanatio: Rulers who called themselves enlightened agreed on the partition; by 1795 Poland had disappeared from the map entirely.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-34#question: On whose behalf did Voltaire campaign in a famous legal case?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-34#explanatio: Calas had been wrongfully executed in Toulouse in 1762; Voltaire secured his rehabilitation and wrote his Treatise on Tolerance about the case.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-35#question: Which idea did Voltaire mock in his novel Candide?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-35#choices.0: That the Earth revolves around the Sun
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-35#choices.1: That all people are born equal
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-35#choices.3: That the world is the best of all possible worlds
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-35#explanatio: The Lisbon earthquake of 1755 had shaken faith in a well-ordered world; the formula of the best of all possible worlds came from Leibniz.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-36#question: Who may make laws according to Rousseau's Social Contract of 1762?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-36#choices.0: Only the king appointed by God
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-36#choices.2: Only the general will of the people
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-36#explanatio: With this Rousseau laid the foundation of popular sovereignty; the book was banned in Paris and Geneva, and the Jacobins later revered him as a prophet of the Revolution.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-37#question: Who edited the Encyclopédie, the great reference work of the Enlightenment?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-37#choices.1: Denis Diderot and Jean le Rond d'Alembert
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-37#explanatio: More than 140 authors wrote for the work, which despite bans and censorship grew to 28 volumes with over 70,000 articles by 1772.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-38#question: What did the Italian Enlightenment thinker Cesare Beccaria campaign for?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-38#choices.1: The abolition of torture and the death penalty
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-38#explanatio: Beccaria's 1764 treatise On Crimes and Punishments influenced rulers such as Catherine II and criminal law reforms throughout Europe.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-39#question: What idea of God did deism hold?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-39#choices.0: God reveals himself above all through miracles and saints
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-39#choices.1: There is no God, only matter
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-39#choices.2: God acts solely through the anointed king
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-39#choices.3: God created the world like a watchmaker and no longer intervenes
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-39#explanatio: Many Enlightenment thinkers sought a rational religion without superstition; deism acknowledged a creator but largely rejected revelation and miracles.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-40#question: Which Jewish philosopher worked for religious tolerance in the Berlin Enlightenment?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-40#explanatio: Mendelssohn was a close friend of Gotthold Ephraim Lessing, who paid tribute to him in the character of Nathan the Wise.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-41#question: Where did Adam Smith see the source of the wealth of nations in 1776?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-41#choices.0: In free trade and the division of labor
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-41#choices.1: In the largest possible stocks of gold and silver
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-41#choices.2: In high protective tariffs on imports
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-41#choices.3: In state manufactories for luxury goods
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-41#explanatio: With The Wealth of Nations Smith criticized mercantilism and became the founder of classical economics.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-42#question: What was shipped from Africa to the Americas in the Atlantic triangular trade?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-42#explanatio: European goods went to Africa, enslaved people to the Americas, and plantation products such as sugar, tobacco and coffee to Europe.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-43#question: What were the first steam engines built after Thomas Newcomen's design from 1712 mainly used for?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-43#explanatio: The engines consumed enormous amounts of coal, which hardly mattered in mining; only Watt's improvement made them economical for factories.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-44#question: With which innovation did James Watt improve the steam engine in 1769?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-44#choices.1: A drive powered by water wheels
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-44#choices.2: A condenser separate from the cylinder
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-44#choices.3: Firing with oil instead of coal
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-44#explanatio: Because the cylinder now stayed hot, fuel consumption fell by about three quarters; from 1775 Watt and Matthew Boulton built engines for factories and mines.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-45#question: Which celestial event was James Cook sent by the Royal Society to observe on Tahiti in 1769?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-45#choices.2: The transit of Venus across the Sun
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-45#explanatio: Such measurements were meant to calculate the distance between the Earth and the Sun; afterwards Cook circumnavigated New Zealand and reached the east coast of Australia in 1770.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-46#question: In which science did Maria Winkelmann conduct research around 1700 despite all the obstacles facing women?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-46#explanatio: Winkelmann observed the sky in Berlin and discovered a comet in 1702, but as a woman she was denied a post at the Academy.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-47#question: Which dynasty ruled China in the 18th century?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-47#explanatio: Under emperors such as Kangxi and Qianlong the Qing empire, founded by the Manchus, reached its greatest extent.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-48#question: Which of these events happened first?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-48#choices.2: The first volume of the Encyclopédie
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-48#choices.3: Watt's patent on the steam engine
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-48#explanatio: Galileo was condemned in 1633, the Principia appeared in 1687, the Encyclopédie from 1751, and Watt's patent followed in 1769.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-49#question: Which event saved Frederick II from looming defeat in the Seven Years' War in 1762?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-49#choices.1: Spain entering the war on Prussia's side
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-49#choices.2: The death of the Russian empress Elizabeth
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-49#explanatio: Her successor Peter III admired Frederick and made peace; Prussia kept Silesia and rose to great-power status.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-50#question: Which city was destroyed by an earthquake, a tsunami and fires on All Saints' Day 1755?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-50#explanatio: Tens of thousands died; the minister Pombal had the city rebuilt to resist earthquakes and the causes investigated scientifically.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-51#question: Which colonial territory did France lose to Great Britain in the Seven Years' War?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-51#explanatio: Great Britain defeated France in North America and India and became the leading colonial power in 1763.
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-52#question: Which composer belongs to the Baroque era?
q-absolutismus-aufklaerung-52#explanatio: Bach and Handel created works that are at the core of European music; Haydn and Mozart followed in the second half of the 18th century.
q-afrikanische-reiche-01#question: Which king of Aksum converted to Christianity in the 4th century?
q-afrikanische-reiche-01#explanation: Ezana adopted Christianity around 330 under the influence of Bishop Frumentius.
q-afrikanische-reiche-02#question: Which ruler of the Mali Empire became famous for his gold-laden pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324?
q-afrikanische-reiche-02#explanation: On his pilgrimage Mansa Musa gave away so much gold in Cairo that the price of gold there fell.
q-afrikanische-reiche-03#question: Which city on the Niger, with the Sankore Mosque and tens of thousands of manuscripts, was a center of Islamic scholarship?
q-afrikanische-reiche-03#explanation: Under Mali and Songhai, Timbuktu was one of the most important cities of learning in Africa.
q-afrikanische-reiche-04#question: Which ruler made the Zulu the strongest power in southeastern Africa from 1816?
q-afrikanische-reiche-04#explanation: Shaka took over the leadership of the Zulu in 1816 and built a powerful army of age regiments.
q-afrikanische-reiche-05#question: In which present-day country are the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela located?
q-afrikanische-reiche-05#explanation: The rock-hewn churches of Lalibela lie in the Ethiopian highlands and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
q-afrikanische-reiche-06#question: In which battle did a Moroccan army with firearms defeat the Songhai Empire in 1591?
q-afrikanische-reiche-06#explanation: At Tondibi near Gao the army of Askia Ishaq II was defeated by the Moroccan musketeers.
q-afrikanische-reiche-07#question: Which king of Kongo complained about the slave trade in letters to the king of Portugal in 1526?
q-afrikanische-reiche-07#explanation: Afonso I wrote to João III that traders were carrying off free subjects and nobles.
q-afrikanische-reiche-08#question: Which female ruler resisted the Portuguese for decades in present-day Angola in the 17th century?
q-afrikanische-reiche-08#explanation: Njinga ruled Ndongo and Matamba and combined war and diplomacy against the colonial power Portugal.
q-afrikanische-reiche-09#choices.0: The sacred symbol of the unity of the Asante Empire
q-afrikanische-reiche-09#choices.1: The throne of the kings of Benin
q-afrikanische-reiche-09#choices.2: A relic in the churches of Lalibela
q-afrikanische-reiche-09#choices.3: An honorary title of the sultans of Kilwa
q-afrikanische-reiche-09#explanation: According to tradition, since Osei Tutu the Golden Stool has embodied the soul and unity of the Asante.
q-afrikanische-reiche-10#question: What was the name of the treaty that the Nubian kingdom of Makuria concluded with Arab Egypt in 652?
q-afrikanische-reiche-10#explanation: The Baqt regulated peace and the exchange of goods and secured Makuria about 600 years of independence.
q-afrikanische-reiche-11#question: Which scholar called for the jihad in 1804 from which the Sokoto Caliphate emerged?
q-afrikanische-reiche-11#explanation: Usman dan Fodio and his followers overthrew the Hausa kings; in 1809 Sokoto became the capital of the caliphate.
q-afrikanische-reiche-12#question: Which Merina king concluded a treaty with Britain in 1817 and banned the export of slaves?
q-afrikanische-reiche-12#explanation: In return for renouncing the slave export, Radama I received British weapons and recognition as king of Madagascar.
q-afrikanische-reiche-13#question: Which empire did the Persian religious founder Mani count, alongside Rome, Persia and Aksum, among the four great empires of the world in the 3rd century?
q-afrikanische-reiche-13#explanation: Mani named China as the fourth great empire; Aksum's place in the list shows the importance of its Red Sea trade.
q-afrikanische-reiche-14#question: Which South Arabian kingdom did King Kaleb of Aksum conquer around 525?
q-afrikanische-reiche-14#explanation: Kaleb marched against the Jewish king Yusuf As'ar of Himyar, who had persecuted the Christians of Najran; around 570 the region fell to the Sasanians.
q-afrikanische-reiche-15#question: Which language is still the liturgical language of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church today?
q-afrikanische-reiche-15#explanation: Ge'ez is attested since the time of Aksum and died out as an everyday language in the Middle Ages; the scripts of Amharic and Tigrinya developed from its script.
q-afrikanische-reiche-16#question: Which city was the capital of the Christian Nubian kingdom of Makuria?
q-afrikanische-reiche-16#explanation: At Dongola the Arab armies were defeated by the Nubian archers in 652; Meroe and Napata, by contrast, were capitals of the older kingdom of Kush.
q-afrikanische-reiche-17#question: What did the Soninke themselves call the empire that Arabic sources call Ghana?
q-afrikanische-reiche-17#explanation: Ghana was originally a ruler's title; the empire of Wagadu lay in the border region of present-day Mauritania and Mali.
q-afrikanische-reiche-18#question: Which commodity in the trans-Saharan trade came from the desert and the north and was exchanged for gold in West Africa?
q-afrikanische-reiche-18#explanation: Salt from the desert mines was so sought after in the south that it was traded for gold; gold, ivory and kola nuts, by contrast, came from the south.
q-afrikanische-reiche-19#question: Where did the geographer al-Bakri write his famous description of the Ghana Empire in 1068?
q-afrikanische-reiche-19#explanation: Al-Bakri never visited West Africa himself but collected merchants' reports in Córdoba; he described a capital made up of a merchants' town and a royal town.
q-afrikanische-reiche-20#question: On which lake was the Kanem-Bornu Empire located?
q-afrikanische-reiche-20#explanation: Kanem lay northeast of Lake Chad; in the 14th century the kings moved their seat to Bornu, west of the lake.
q-afrikanische-reiche-21#question: What is special about the walls of Great Zimbabwe?
q-afrikanische-reiche-21#choices.0: They were built of sun-dried mud bricks
q-afrikanische-reiche-21#choices.1: They are made of carefully stacked granite blocks without mortar
q-afrikanische-reiche-21#choices.2: They consist of fired bricks with lime mortar
q-afrikanische-reiche-21#choices.3: They were built as wooden palisades on earthworks
q-afrikanische-reiche-21#explanation: The mortarless granite walls reach up to eleven metres in height; the Great Enclosure is the largest precolonial structure south of the Sahara.
q-afrikanische-reiche-22#question: Which city is regarded in Yoruba tradition as the place where the world was created?
q-afrikanische-reiche-22#explanation: Ife is also considered the place of origin of the Yoruba royal families; naturalistic heads of copper alloy and terracotta were made there between the 12th and 15th centuries.
q-afrikanische-reiche-23#question: What is the ground plan of Bete Giyorgis, the most famous of the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela?
q-afrikanische-reiche-23#explanation: The Church of St George was carved downward into the volcanic rock and sits in a deep pit; the complex was meant to represent a new Jerusalem.
q-afrikanische-reiche-24#question: To whom did Ethiopia's Solomonic dynasty, which ruled from 1270, trace its descent?
q-afrikanische-reiche-24#choices.2: King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba
q-afrikanische-reiche-24#explanation: The dynasty claimed descent from Menelik, the legendary son of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba; with interruptions it ruled until Haile Selassie was overthrown in 1974.
q-afrikanische-reiche-25#question: In which book was the legend of the Ethiopian kings' descent from Solomon written down in detail in the 14th century?
q-afrikanische-reiche-25#explanation: Kebra Nagast means Glory of the Kings; it closely tied the monarchy to the Ethiopian Church.
q-afrikanische-reiche-26#question: What are the hereditary singers and storytellers of West Africa who still perform the Epic of Sundiata called?
q-afrikanische-reiche-26#explanation: Griots pass on genealogies, praise songs and the history of ruling families orally and also served as advisers at royal courts.
q-afrikanische-reiche-27#question: Which traveller visited the Swahili city of Kilwa around 1331 and praised it as one of the most beautiful cities in the world?
q-afrikanische-reiche-27#explanation: Ibn Battuta travelled through much of the Islamic world; Kilwa owed its wealth to gold from the Zimbabwe plateau, which reached the coast via Sofala.
q-afrikanische-reiche-28#question: Which map of 1375 shows Mansa Musa holding a gold nugget as ruler of West Africa?
q-afrikanische-reiche-28#explanation: The Catalan Atlas was made on Majorca and shows how much Mali's wealth in gold impressed even Europe after Mansa Musa's pilgrimage.
q-afrikanische-reiche-29#question: Which empire did Shona rulers establish in the north on the Zambezi around 1430, after the decline of Great Zimbabwe?
q-afrikanische-reiche-29#explanation: Its rulers bore the title Mwene Mutapa and controlled the gold and ivory trade; in 1629 the empire became dependent on Portugal.
q-afrikanische-reiche-30#question: Which works of art did British troops loot from the royal palace of Benin in 1897?
q-afrikanische-reiche-30#explanation: The commemorative heads and relief plaques were made by guilds of casters for the ancestral altars of the Obas; their return is still being negotiated today.
q-afrikanische-reiche-31#explanation: The Alaafin ruled together with the council of nobles, the Oyo Mesi, which could even force him to commit suicide; Oyo's strength rested on its large cavalry.
q-afrikanische-reiche-32#question: What was the Hausa city of Kano especially famous for?
q-afrikanische-reiche-32#explanation: Besides its indigo cloth, Kano was known for leather goods; in the 15th century Muhammad Rumfa founded the great Kurmi market there.
q-afrikanische-reiche-33#question: Which city was the capital of the Songhai Empire?
q-afrikanische-reiche-33#explanation: From Gao, Sunni Ali conquered Timbuktu in 1468 and later Djenné; Niani, by contrast, is regarded as a capital of the Mali Empire.
q-afrikanische-reiche-34#question: Which Portuguese navigator reached the mouth of the Congo in 1483 and made contact with the Kingdom of Kongo?
q-afrikanische-reiche-34#explanation: After this contact, envoys travelled to Lisbon, and in 1491 King Nzinga a Nkuwu was baptized in Mbanza Kongo.
q-afrikanische-reiche-35#question: Which Muslim sultanate overran large parts of Christian Ethiopia from 1529 under Imam Ahmad Gran?
q-afrikanische-reiche-35#explanation: Ahmad Gran won with Ottoman firearms but was killed in 1543 at Wayna Daga fighting Emperor Galawdewos and a Portuguese relief force.
q-afrikanische-reiche-36#question: What did the Moroccan sultan Ahmad al-Mansur aim to achieve with his campaign against Songhai in 1591?
q-afrikanische-reiche-36#choices.0: The conversion of the Songhai to Islam
q-afrikanische-reiche-36#choices.1: Protection of the pilgrim routes to Mecca
q-afrikanische-reiche-36#choices.2: Control of West Africa's sources of gold
q-afrikanische-reiche-36#choices.3: New land for farmers to settle
q-afrikanische-reiche-36#explanation: Al-Mansur wanted to gain access to West African gold; Songhai had long been Muslim, and the hoped-for quantities of gold never reached Morocco.
q-afrikanische-reiche-37#question: Which scholar from Timbuktu was deported to Marrakesh after the Moroccan conquest?
q-afrikanische-reiche-37#explanation: Ahmad Baba wrote more than 40 works and was only allowed to return in 1608; the manuscript institute in Timbuktu is named after him today.
q-afrikanische-reiche-38#question: Which king of Kongo was killed in 1665 at the Battle of Mbwila against a Portuguese army?
q-afrikanische-reiche-38#explanation: António I's head was taken to Luanda; afterwards Kongo broke apart for decades in civil wars between rival noble families.
q-afrikanische-reiche-39#question: From which city did the Asantehene rule their empire?
q-afrikanische-reiche-39#explanation: Osei Tutu was ruler of Kumasi before he united the Akan states and became the first Asantehene; Abomey was the capital of Dahomey.
q-afrikanische-reiche-40#question: What was a distinctive feature of the army of Dahomey?
q-afrikanische-reiche-40#explanation: Europeans called Dahomey's women warriors Amazons; the kingdom captured the slave port of Ouidah in 1727.
q-afrikanische-reiche-41#question: Which daughter of Usman dan Fodio worked as a poet and promoter of women's education in the Sokoto Caliphate?
q-afrikanische-reiche-41#explanation: Nana Asma'u spoke four languages, wrote poems on religion and history and advised her brother Muhammad Bello.
q-afrikanische-reiche-42#question: What were the women teachers called whom Nana Asma'u trained to pass on knowledge in verse to rural women?
q-afrikanische-reiche-42#explanation: The Yan Taru network brought religious and practical knowledge to the villages; in northern Nigeria Nana Asma'u is still regarded as a model for women's education.
q-afrikanische-reiche-43#question: Which way of fighting did Shaka introduce among the Zulu?
q-afrikanische-reiche-43#choices.0: Disciplined close combat with a short stabbing spear and a large shield
q-afrikanische-reiche-43#choices.1: Mounted combat with bow and arrow
q-afrikanische-reiche-43#explanation: Shaka also organized the warriors into age-based regiments that lived in their own barracks; he was murdered by his half-brothers in 1828.
q-afrikanische-reiche-44#question: Which present-day state grew out of the kingdom that Moshoeshoe founded on the mountain plateau of Thaba Bosiu during the Mfecane?
q-afrikanische-reiche-44#explanation: On Thaba Bosiu Moshoeshoe gathered refugees of the Mfecane and created the kingdom of the Basotho, from which Lesotho emerged.
q-afrikanische-reiche-45#question: Which queen banned Christianity in Madagascar in 1835 and expelled most foreigners?
q-afrikanische-reiche-45#explanation: Ranavalona I, the widow of Radama I, saw the missionaries as a threat to independence; in 1845 her army repelled a British-French attack on Toamasina.
q-afrikanische-reiche-46#question: Which plantation crop did Sultan Said bin Sultan have grown on Zanzibar by enslaved labourers?
q-afrikanische-reiche-46#explanation: Around 1840 Sultan Said moved his residence from Muscat to Zanzibar, which also became the largest slave market in East Africa.
q-afrikanische-reiche-47#question: Which power stormed the fortress of Magdala belonging to the Ethiopian emperor Tewodros II in 1868?
q-afrikanische-reiche-47#explanation: Tewodros had imprisoned British envoys; when Magdala fell, he took his own life.
q-afrikanische-reiche-48#question: Under which Zulu king did the Zulu defeat a British force at Isandlwana in 1879?
q-afrikanische-reiche-48#explanation: Isandlwana was one of the heaviest defeats of a European army in Africa; after the defeat at Ulundi in July 1879, Cetshwayo was captured.
q-afrikanische-reiche-49#question: What does the term Swahili refer to?
q-afrikanische-reiche-49#choices.0: A Bantu language and culture of the East African trading cities
